clue.text: Kentish meat preserver's locker

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE
someone who cures bacon or ham by salting and smoking is a curer

explanation.surface: A Kent butcher who salts meat keeps it in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'), joining the wordplay to the definition. A locker is something that makes things more secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that locks makes a door or box safer, so a locker is a thing that makes fast.

clue.text: Wee cut

definitions.meaning: British slang: to urinate, or the act of urinating
a long gash made with a blade

explanation.surface: A tiny injury.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a trip to urinate is called this, and a sweeping knife wound has the same name.

clue.text: With swerving action, left and right, so I ran the party as footballer

indicators.note: a footballer's swerving run twists these letters into a new order

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A winger cuts left and right with a jinking run, dominating the occasion like the star he is.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is ACTION, L, R, SOIRAN and DO, sixteen letters rearranged by 'swerving'. The Portuguese forward was famous for exactly this sort of dribbling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese forward, once of Manchester United and Real Madrid, is among the most famous soccer players ever.

clue.text: See 20
Something dubious and fishy?

definitions.meaning: a false lead that diverts attention from the truth
a kipper, a herring cured until it turns reddish-brown

explanation.surface: Something smells off about this.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue in a mystery is named after the smoked kipper once dragged to throw hounds off a scent.

clue.text: Fruity, but shrivelled up, concubine?

definitions.meaning: a dried grape, a piece of fruit that has shrivelled
a wife or consort of an Eastern ruler

explanation.surface: A once-saucy harem favourite has gone wrinkled with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' reads as 'saucy' in the surface; in the first definition it stands for a piece of fruit. The second definition is the sultan's consort, loosely called a concubine.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedless dried grape bears this name, as does the wife of a Muslim sovereign.

clue.text: This might be nonsense

indicators.note: the word before could become, once rearranged, the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that the statement in front of them is worth anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' says that the letters of 'This' could be rearranged into the answer, a vulgar word for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar slang for drivel or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Union man was defeated Wednesday's solution boxing unknown boxer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Union man was defeated Wednesday's solution boxing unknown boxer'. The parse is LO(Y ALI)ST with 'was defeated' as LOST; 'Wednesday's solution' has no job and looks like the newspaper's caption for the previous day's grid swept into the clue by OCR, which is more than a 3-letter misread.
annotationWithheld.clue: Union man was defeated Wednesday's solution boxing unknown boxer

clue.text: See 25
See 14
Principle of a team order

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a side in football or cricket
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A side's manager lays down a rule of behaviour for the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: Order of Merit (OM) is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth taken as a basic premise.

clue.text: She milks charity after huge amount sent back

indicators.note: the charity piece comes after the reversed piece in the answer
something sent back goes the reverse way, so the word is written from its end

parts.note: a myriad is a countless number
aid is help given to those in need

explanation.surface: A fundraiser exploits a vast donation that was returned to the donor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' gives DAIRYM, which 'after' puts in front of AID. 'She milks' looks like a verb of exploitation, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed on a farm to milk the cows and make butter.

clue.text: A requirement when brewing up trouble

definitions.meaning: making a pot of tea needs liquid at boiling point
to be in difficulty, as in a scrape

explanation.surface: Something is needed when stirring up mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing up' looks like plotting mischief; in British usage it is making tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling liquid is needed for tea, and an idiom for being in a fix uses the same phrase.

clue.text: 26 I attached to organ

indicators.note: the I is fixed on the end of the organ word

parts.note: a lung is a breathing organ

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle says a garment sticks to a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is the answer to 26 Across, an Asian garment worn wrapped round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong-like cloth wrapped round the hips, worn by men in India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Seductive space traveller's captivating greeting overcoming her

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that overcomes another sits above it
a thing that captivates holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a comet travels through space
hi is a casual hello
taken as written

explanation.surface: An alien's charming hello wins over a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' gives COMEHIT. In a down entry, 'overcoming' means sitting on top, so that comes before HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A look or manner that is alluring and invites someone closer.

clue.text: Naughty fun with farmer's tool, entertaining boy wielding hammer, ending in conflict

indicators.note: a host who entertains holds guests within, so the tool word holds the rest

parts.note: a sickle is a curved blade for cutting crops

indicators.note: the boy holds the hammer word in his grip

parts.note: a lad is a boy
to pan is to criticise harshly, to hammer

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A frolic with a farm implement and a boy swinging a mallet ends in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wielding' gives LAPAND, and 'ending in' adds T. 'entertaining' sets those inside the tool word after its first letter. 'hammer' is a verb meaning slate, not a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned jocular British phrase for kissing and cuddling.

clue.text: Kit joins bash in sleazy establishment

parts.note: a team's strip is its kit or uniform
to club is to hit, to bash

explanation.surface: A football uniform is combined with a beating in a seedy dive.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sports team's strip is its playing kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue where performers undress, the sort of seedy place this describes.

clue.text: Might one carry bad woman, old, most foul, into embrace of good man?

indicators.note: the pieces go into the arms of the good man, held inside him

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, decent person

indicators.note: the letters of the word are fouled up into a different order

explanation.surface: A question asks whether a rotten old woman could be taken into a decent man's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' gives OMST, which with O goes 'into embrace of' the good man after his first two letters. The bad woman is a witch, who flies on what the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch is pictured riding through the sky on a long-handled sweeping brush.

clue.text: Neutral island warlike, seizing power

indicators.note: the warlike word grabs the next piece and holds it inside

parts.note: martial means warlike
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A belligerent island grabs control yet claims to take no side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' puts P inside MARTIAL, after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Not favouring either side; unbiased.

clue.text: Might campers use this? The Kid is able to

parts.note: Billy the Kid was the American outlaw
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A question about camping kit, then a remark that an outlaw is capable.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text has a stray 'a' before 'The Kid' that the printed clue does not have.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin pot with a lid and wire handle for boiling water over a campfire.

clue.text: One retired after organisation changed direction

indicators.note: the letters are organised, set out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A pensioner took a new course once the firm was restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after organisation' rearranges the ten letters of ONE RETIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned to face or aim another way; realigned.

clue.text: Sword needing point to 1 Down

parts.note: E (east) is a compass point
the answer to 1 Down is British slang for a wee, which is a pee

explanation.surface: A blade must be sharpened to a tip to slice.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Down is read in its 'wee' sense here, not its 'cut' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A light fencing blade used in duelling sport.

clue.text: Personality often cursing, finding way through heavy force, perhaps

indicators.note: the way piece runs through the middle of the heavy

parts.note: a goon is a heavy, a hired thug
RD is short for road, a way
to ram is to force
say means for example, perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone who swears a lot passes a thug, perhaps with violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' gives GORDON. The TV chef is famous for swearing in the kitchen, and 'heavy' is the noun for a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish celebrity chef is notorious for foul-mouthed outbursts on TV.

clue.text: Student through which things seen to pass?

definitions.text: through which things seen to pass?
definitions.meaning: the opening in the eye's iris that light enters

explanation.surface: A learner sees through things.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolchild is called this, and so is the dark centre of the eye.

clue.text: Exclusively given access to the smallest room

definitions.meaning: let in on a secret, as in 'party to'
a toilet, especially an outdoor one

explanation.surface: Only a few may enter the tiniest space in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The smallest room' is a British euphemism for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in on a secret uses this word, which also names an outside lavatory.

clue.text: Weight I record, entering score in reverse

indicators.note: the first pieces enter, going inside the turned word
the word for score is written back to front

parts.note: a mark is a score given in a test
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A dieter logs results that show a backward step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' gives KRAM, and 'entering' sends I and LOG into it. 'Weight' is a fair definition because in everyday use the metric unit of mass is treated as a weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of mass, a thousand grams.

clue.text: Fruit among bananas

indicators.note: slang for crazy, so the letters go mad and change order

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit sits in a bunch of bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is slang for crazy, so it rearranges AMONG; it is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit with sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: I didn't quite get that further invitation

definitions.meaning: a request to repeat what was said
asking someone to visit once more

explanation.surface: A host missed the reply to a second invite.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'pardon?' and asking a guest back use the same two words.

clue.text: Colin terribly unwilling to reveal Asian garment

indicators.note: done terribly, the name's letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: loth means reluctant, unwilling

explanation.surface: Colin is very reluctant to show off his Eastern clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges COLIN into LOINC.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of fabric wrapped about the hips, the sole garb in hot regions of South Asia.

clue.text: Stoop to read aloud Hans Christian Andersen, perhaps

indicators.note: what is read out is heard, not seen, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: the fairy-tale writer was from Denmark, a Dane

explanation.surface: Lower yourself to recite fairy tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Andersen as one example of a Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend, lowering oneself to do something.

clue.text: Sexy diva has you spinning inside head

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the head word

parts.note: bonce is British slang for head

indicators.note: the word spins round, so it reads backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A glamorous singer makes your head spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' gives EY, which 'inside' places after the first letter of the head word. Bonce is everyday British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The American R&B superstar, known for her glamorous image.

clue.text: See 2
